  Tuesday, August 15, 2023

  Recommended Action: Approval

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 15, 2023  2
   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JULY 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-2024 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for July 2023.

  D. RESOLUTION NOS. 23-49 AND 23-50 SETTING THE RATE AND AMOUNT
  NECESSARY FOR THE 2023-24 FISCAL YEAR RETIREMENT LEVY

  The City’s retirement costs are funded by a special property tax levy
  authorized by the voters in 1948. The special property tax levy approved by
  the voters requires the City Council to annually establish a tax rate sufficient
  to meet the City’s obligations to the state employees’ retirement system.
  Based on the assessed valuation prepared by the Auditor Controller and the
  recommended continued levy of 14 cents per $100 of assessed property
  value, the amount to be generated is estimated at $9,531,351 for Fiscal Year
  2023-2024. This levy, along with the current fund balance in the Retirement
  Fund, will be sufficient to cover the retirement costs, budgeted at $9,886,942
  for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-49, setting
  the tax rate at 14 cents per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution No. 23-
  50, fixing the amount of property taxes to be generated for the City
  employee’s retirement cost for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

  E. AGREEMENT WITH HDL COMPANIES TO PERFORM A STUDY OF THE
  CITY’S BUSINESS LICENSE TAX ORDINANCE IN THE AMOUNT OF $25,000

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 15, 2023  3
   The City’s business license code has not had a significant update for decades
  and includes outdated fee amounts which need to be reviewed and amended
  as necessary. Staff obtained proposals from qualified firms to perform an
  analysis of the City’s business license tax structure to modernize the business
  license tax code and propose methods to simplify our tax structure and
  generate additional local funds while increasing the equity of the business
  license tax. Funds to conduct a business license tax ordinance study are
  included in the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 general fund budget. The proposed cost
  for HDL to perform a business license tax ordinance study is $20,000 plus
  $5,000 for a second study update for a total amount of $25,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into an agreement with HDL Companies for a business license tax ordinance
  study.

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 691 RELATING TO ELECTRONIC AND PAPERLESS FILING
  OF FAIR POLITICAL PRACTICES COMMISSION (FPPC) CAMPAIGN
  DISCLOSURE STATEMENTS AND STATEMENTS OF ECONOMIC INTERESTS
  – INTRODUCTION

  Ordinance No. 691 would require electronic filing of campaign finance
  statements and Statements of Economic Interests. The cost to add electronic
  filing of campaign finance statements is $1900 annually. Funds have been
  appropriated in the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Adopted Budget City Clerk’s Office
  budget (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council introduce Ordinance No. 691, adding
  Chapter 40 “Electronic and Paperless Filing of Fair Political Practices
  Commission Campaign Disclosure Statements and Statements of Economic
  Interests” to Title III “Administration” of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, for
  first reading by title only, waive future reading, and schedule the second
  reading and adoption for the next regularly-scheduled City Council meeting.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 15, 2023  4
   G. RESOLUTION NO. 23-47 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 600 BLOCK OF SYCAMORE DRIVE

  The Public Works Department received a request from Alex Islas, resident at
  613 Sycamore Drive, for a temporary street closure. The purpose of this
  request is to hold a block party on Thursday, August 17, 2023, on the 600
  block of Sycamore Drive from 5:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-47
  authorizing closure on the 600 block of Sycamore Drive between Hermosa
  Drive and Duane Avenue from 5:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. on Thursday, August 17,
  2023.

  H. RESOLUTION NO. 23-48 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 300 BLOCK OF BRIDGE STREET

  The Public Works Department received a request from Raymond Lieu, resident
  at 329 Bridge Street, for a temporary street closure. The purpose of this
  request is to hold a block party on Saturday, September 2, 2023, on the 300
  block of Bridge Street from 3:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-48
  authorizing closure on Bridge Street between Sycamore Drive to the end of
  the cul-de-sac from 3:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Saturday, September 2, 2023.

  I. RESOLUTION NO. 23-55 – RESOLUTION FOR TEMPORARY STREET
  CLOSURES DURING BLOCK PARTIES

  Each year, the City of San Gabriel receives several applications from residents
  to host block parties in the community. Over the past few years, several
  applicants have been rejected for failing to meet the lengthy six-week

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 15, 2023  5
   requirement, leaving residents unhappy and frustrated. Most of the
  applications are repeat applicants and the City Council has historically
  approved all residential block party requests. There is no fiscal impact related
  to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-55
  authorizing the Public Works Director to review and approve future residential
  block party applications.

  J. PURCHASE OF SELF-CONTAINED BREATHING APPARATUS IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $473,061.71

  The San Gabiel Fire Department is in need of replacing its Self-Contained
  Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) due to end of service life of the Honeywell Titan
  Model currently in service. Fire Department personnel have evaluated
  different models of SCBA meeting National Fire Protection Agency Standards
  and have determined that the MSA G1 SCBA best fulfils our current and future
  needs. The total purchase price, including tax, is $473,461.71. The SCBA
  replacement purchase is approved as a Special Project in the Fiscal Year 2023-
  2024 budget and funded by the general fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the issuance of a purchase
  order in the amount of $473,461.71 to LN Curtis, Incorporated for the
  purchase of twenty-eight MSA G1 SCBA.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. APPEAL (APPEAL NO. 23-001) PLANNING PROJECTS NOS. CUP23-003
  AND VAR23-001
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT AND VARIANCE (535 WEST ROSES ROAD)

  The application for a conditional use permit and variance for 535 West Roses
  Road has been withdrawn. The Public Hearing for this item has been canceled.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 15, 2023  6
   B. APPEAL (APPEAL NO. 23-002) OF PLANNING CASE NO. PPD21-008
  PRECISE PLAN OF DESIGN (330 WEST LAS TUNAS DRIVE)
  APPELLANT: LOZEAU DRURY, LLP / SUPPORTERS ALLIANCE FOR
  ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSIBILITY (SAFER)

  This appeal application (APPEAL No. 23-002) is to appeal the Design Review
  Commission’s decision to approve a Precise Plan of Design (PPD21-008) for a
  proposed medical office building located at 330 West Las Tunas Drive. The
  proposed project would demolish the existing one-story medical office
  building and construct a new five-story, 74,490 square foot medical office
  building on a 63,779 square foot (approximately 1.46 acres) lot. The subject
  property is zoned MF (Medical Facilities) under the Mission District Specific
  Plan and has a General Plan Land Use Designation of Medical Facilities. There
  is no fiscal impact associated with the consideration of an appeal.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  ADOPT a Resolution DENYING the appeal and upholding the APPROVAL of
  Resolution No. 23-04 for Planning Case No. PPD21-008 for a Precise Plan of
  Design at 330 West Las Tunas Drive, subject to the recommended conditions
  of approval.

  Alternative Options for Consideration

  ➢ Option 1 – APPROVE the appeal, make the findings, and direct staff to
  return with a Resolution for the DENIAL of Planning Case No. PPD 21-008
  at the next regularly scheduled City Council meeting on September 5,
  2023.

  Option 1 would mean that the project would not be constructed.

  ➢ Option 2 – DENY the appeal, MODIFY in whole or in part, the action of
  the Design Review Commission, make the findings, and direct staff to
  return with an amended Resolution for the APPROVAL of the Planning
  Case No. PPD 21-008 at the next regularly scheduled Council meeting on
  September 5, 2023.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 15, 2023  7
   Option 2 would mean approving the project with modifications in
  response to the City Council direction.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. PICKLEBALL DISCUSSION – POTENTIAL AWARD OF A CONSTRUCTION
  CONTRACT NO. 23-08 IN THE AMOUNT OF $90,500, PLUS A $9,050
  CONTINGENCY TO COMMERCIAL PAVING AND COATING FOR THE
  CONSTRUCTION OF NEW CONCRETE SLAB FOR PICKEBALL COURTS AT
  SMITH PARK

  During the July 18, 2023 City Council Meeting, staff presented a construction
  contract for a new pickleball court at Smith Park. At that meeting, public
  comments and a petition were presented speaking against the construction of
  the new court. After much deliberation, the City Council requested to have the
  item come back at a future meeting. Should the Council choose Option 1,
  Parks Development Impact Fee funds in the amount of $90,500 plus a $9,050
  contingency will be utilized to fund the construction of four new pickleball
  courts. The funds were appropriated in the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 budget and
  will be carried to the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 budget. Should the City Council
  choose the construction of a pickleball court at another location, staff would
  bring an item forward to include construction/resurfacing costs for the
  approved location.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Depending on the
  option selected by the Council, project is exempt under following exemptions:
  Class 1 (e)(2)(A)(B)Existing Facilities, Class 3 New Construction of Small
  Structures or Class 11 Accessory Structures.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the addition of the pickleball
  court at Smith Park in the proposed location as indicated above, and approve
  construction Contract No. 23-08, authorizing the City Manager to sign all
  documents necessary to execute the contract.

 7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 15, 2023  8

MINUTES OF AUGUST 15, 2023

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at

  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, and announced that Vice Mayor Wu was
  unable to attend the meeting.

  B. APPEAL (APPEAL NO. 23-002) OF PLANNING CASE NO. PPD21-008 PRECISE

  APPELLANT: LOZEAU DRURY, LLP / SUPPORTERS ALLIANCE FOR
  ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSIBILITY (SAFER)

  Mayor Harrington opened the public hearing.

  City Attorney Lemieux noted that only four City Council members were present and
  received agreement from both parties to proceed.

  Senior Planner Christine Song made the staff presentation.

  Robert Montano, Project Manager, Adept Development and Architecture,
  representing the applicant, presented the proposed project.

I  Jordan Sisson, Attorney, representing appellant Supporters Alliance for
  Environmental Responsibility (SAFER), presented the appeal. Chief City Clerk Clark
  read a comment submitted by SAFER representative Victoria Yundt.

  The Applicant's representative presented a rebuttal to the appellant's comments.

  The appellant's representative presented a clarification to his previous comments.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  August 15, 2023
   Dr. Kyle Wong, L-Likon, LLC, spoke in support of the appeal and against approval

  Reza Bonachea Mohamadzadah, Attorneys for Southwest Mountain States
  Regional Council of Carpenters, provided comments advocating workforce
  requirements for the project.
  Richard Burns, resident, member of the Southwest Mountain States Regional
  Council of Carpenters, stated the Council's request for workforce requirements on
  the project.

I  Mayor Harrington closed the public hearing.

  Discussion included the purpose of the Mission District Specific Plan; no next step
  if Council denies the project; the only item for Council to consider is whether
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) requirements were properly followed;
  use of the parking lot is a private agreement between the applicant and the
  property owner; the City's CEQA consultant's methodology (presented by Eddie
  Torres, Department Manager, Michael Baker International); CEQA in-fill exemption
  details; construction-phasing timeline; and that the City Council must make all five
  findings to approve the project as it went to the Design Review Commission (DRC),

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to adopt Resolution No. 23-51 denying the appeal and upholding the
  approval of Resolution No. 23 -04 for Planning Case No. PPD21-008 for a Precise
  Plan of Design at 330 West Las Tunas Drive, subject to the recommended
  conditions of approval.

  RECESS AND RECONVENE

  The meeting was recessed at 9:58 P.M. and reconvened at 10:08 P.M. with all Council
  Members present except Vice Mayor Wu.

  Discussion included that the benefits outweigh the concerns for the most residents;
  noise mitigation; enforcement of operating hours; benefit of having the distinction
  of being a pickleball-friendly city; recent replacement of the tennis court light timer
  for better accuracy on timing; plans for small improvements to the pool over time
  funded by the City's General Fund and the estimated cost of various pool repairs;
  the proposed construction of the pickleball court would be funded by
  Development Impact Fees; park restrooms were recently renovated but get
  vandalized frequently; security cameras to be installed at the park; the Police
  Department has received one pickleball noise complaint in the last year; feasibility
  of moving trees; open space versus dedicated space; importance of the area
  dedicated to local tribes; feasibility of use of school facilities; displacing use instead

I  of eliminating use; being inclusive of all in the community; Tongva Memorial would
  not be moved; and economic and health benefits relative to pickleball.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to approve the addition of the pickleball court at Smith Park in the proposed
  location and approve construction Contract No. 23-08, authorizing the City
  Manager to sign all documents necessary to execute the contract.
